subject: social_studies
concept: Understanding that a group works better when everyone cooperates rather than only thinking of themselves
source_inspiration: original content, connecting to Tokkatsu-style group-cooperation principles — not sourced from any external text

exercise.concrete: Student completes a simple group task that only works if everyone cooperates
exercise.pictorial: Student compares a cooperative group scene to an uncooperative one and their different outcomes
exercise.abstract: Student explains what happened differently when the group cooperated versus when they didn't

misconception_flags: believes a group task would succeed just as well with only one person doing all the work

interest_binding: exercise regenerated using student's stated interest profile
